label: The runtime mirrored hook dirs are symlinks, not byte-identical copies: .claude/hooks holds 30 symlinks and 1 regular file, the .js/.ts pairs are symlinks into system-spec-kit runtime and dist, and a sweep of .claude/.codex/.cursor/.devin/.pi/.opencode/.skilled/hooks found zero dangling links. Nothing can drift by content and no sync check is owed, so the mirror layer is rejected as a cut candidate.
verify: find .claude/hooks -maxdepth 1 -type l | wc -l -> 30; find .claude/hooks -maxdepth 1 -type f | wc -l -> 1; dangling sweep -> empty

label: 181 runtime adapter sources under .skilled/hooks/*/{claude,codex,cursor,devin,dsh,opencode,pi}/ share one module that exports exactly two functions, readStdin and parseJsonFailOpen; 49 non-test files reference it and 132 do not, so settings-JSON shape, event names, decision JSON and exit codes are re-implemented per adapter. Collapsing to one file would break the feature (protocols genuinely differ), so the cut is to extend the shared module over the runtime-agnostic half; the measurable cost today is that the 3-second stdin deadline fix had to be re-landed per surface and is still not universal.
release: shared adapter arrived with c33f9d1984, first tag v4.0.0.4; adapters accumulated across the v4 line
confidence: medium-high on counts, medium on copy-paste characterisation

label: Two hook sources bypass the shared 3-second stdin deadline with a blocking readFileSync(0, 'utf8'): ask-surface-stop.cjs:83 on the Claude turn-end path and ask-surface-guard/lib/advisory-stop.cjs:44. The deadline is real and tested (hook-adapter-shared.cjs:29, c33f9d1984) but defeated on the surface added last (a8cedfbfb0, first tag v4.0.2.0). Impact is bounded by whether the runtime closes stdin; the failure mode is a hung turn end, not a wrong decision.
confidence: high on code, medium on runtime impact
verify: timeout 5 bash -c 'sleep 60 | node .skilled/hooks/ask-surface-guard/claude/ask-surface-stop.cjs'; exit 124 demonstrates no deadline (not executed this iteration)

label: hook-flags is not four copies: hook-flags.cjs (302 lines) is the engine with module.exports at :286, hook-flags.mjs (25 lines) and hook-flags.ts (55 lines) are thin re-export shims justified by module format, and only hook-flags.sh (113 lines) re-implements the flag table in shell. The shell table is the single genuine duplication and its risk is asymmetric - a stale table makes shell hooks silently disagree with every JS hook about whether a concern is enabled, with no test comparing the two.
release: shell variant predates the v4 line; .mjs/.ts shims landed 2026-10-25

label: The 5637-line Python advisor is not vestigial and the delete-Python cut is rejected: four live consumers remain after the MCP removal - the OpenCode advisor plugin (.opencode/plugins/system-skill-advisor.js:153), the doctor hub check (parent-skill-check.cjs:130), the doctor skill surface (sk-skill-surface.cjs:73 with error paths at :972/:983) and create:skill-parent's --emit-routing-projection (create-skill-parent-auto.yaml:240). The real over-engineering is two scorers under one name, since canon still defines routingClass 'lexical' as scoring in skill_advisor.py (system-deep-loop/mode-registry.json:12) while the skill also ships a Node CLI; the fix is one authority delegating to the other.
release: MCP removal in v4.0.0.0/v4.0.0.16; these callers survived it
confidence: high on callers, medium on the two-scorer framing

label: leaf-scopes.json is a second place to say one thing for a single-mode skill: leaf-manifest.config.json:4 already declares the five leafRoots for the one mode system-skill-advisor, and leaf-scopes.json then lists 8 packet-relative paths for that same mode. The consumer is real (generate-leaf-manifest.cjs:346, gate at pre-commit:495) and the manifest is regenerated and validated, so this is a candidate cut rather than a confirmed one - whether the generator treats the file as optional for a single-mode skill was not read (47f91f9135, first tag v4.0.1.0).
verify: node .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-skill/scripts/generate-leaf-manifest.cjs --check .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor with leaf-scopes.json unset in a scratch copy

label: Carried question closed: hook-flags.env is gitignored (.gitignore:389) and untracked, so its divergence from hook-flags.env.example is by design. The live file activates 5 flag names (SYSTEM_SESSION_RELAUNCH_ENABLED=1, SYSTEM_SESSION_RELAUNCH_CLAUDE_ENABLED=0, SESSION_RELAUNCH_NOTIFY_HOPS=1, and the two validation-skip flags) where the example comments everything, and it never mentions SYSTEM_ASK_SURFACE_DISABLED, which appears only commented at hook-flags.env.example:26 - so the ask-surface guard is enabled on this machine and f-iter006-001 is reachable, not dead.

Introduction tags by git tag --contains: relaunch stop-arm b830fd0276 -> v4.0.0.13; ask-surface-stop a8cedfbfb0 -> v4.0.2.0; stdin-deadline test c33f9d1984 -> v4.0.0.4; leaf-scopes 47f91f9135 -> v4.0.1.0; hooks/dist-freshness check 330427cf30 -> v4.0.0.0. Three distinct introduction releases for one hook cluster, which is why the deadline fix is uneven.

Method correction recorded rather than hidden: the first stdin-bypass scan used readFileSync\(0\) and returned a count of 1 pointing at the shared helper itself, which was wrong because readFileSync(0, 'utf8') has a comma after the 0. The corrected pattern found the two real bypass sites. The earlier number is discarded.

direction: Cut the per-runtime mirrored hook directories (.claude/hooks, .codex/hooks, .cursor/hooks, .devin/hooks) as duplicated copies
reason: They are symlinks, not copies: 30 of 31 entries in .claude/hooks are symlinks, the .js/.ts pairs are symlinks into system-spec-kit runtime and dist, and a sweep of all six runtime roots plus .skilled/hooks found zero dangling links. A symlink has one content so it cannot drift, and a rename surfaces as a dangling link which does not currently exist. There is nothing to collapse and no sync check is missing.

direction: Delete the Python advisor (runtime/scripts/skill_advisor.py, 5637 lines) as a leftover from before the Node scorer
reason: Four live consumers depend on it - OpenCode plugin, doctor hub check, doctor skill surface, create:skill-parent projection emit. Deleting it removes the OpenCode advisor, the doctor hub-gap rows and the projection emit. The cost is two scorers under one name, not a dead implementation.

direction: Treat the four hook-flags.{cjs,mjs,ts,sh} files as four duplicate implementations to collapse into one
reason: Three are one implementation plus two module-format shims (25 and 55 lines). Only the 113-line shell file re-implements the table, and CJS/ESM/TS consumers cannot import each other without a shim, so only the shell table is a legitimate cut.
